newsitem.title: USA: Federal judge dismisses suit vs tobacco companies.
newsitem.headline: Federal judge dismisses suit vs tobacco companies.

text.p: LOUISVILLE, Ky., March 13 - Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp said on Thursday a U.S. Federal judge in New York dismissed an individual product liability lawsuit filed against Brown and other tobacco companies, a case which included federal racketeering claims.

Brown said the court, in Rhera LePaw, et.al., vs. B.A.T Industries, et.al., threw out the plaintiffs' claims that tobacco companies had engaged in racketeering, ruling that "claims for personal injuries or emotional distress are not cognizable under RICO."
The court rejected plaintiffs' argument that they could recover monetary expenses incurred in purchasing cigarettes because of their alleged addiction to smoking.
The court declined to rule on plaintiffs' state-law claims, leaving open the possibility plaintiffs could reassert those claims in state court.
Other defendants in the case included Philip Morris, R.J. Reynolds, Lorillard, Brooke Group and the Tobacco Institute.
